name: kit_d
prompt:
A sheet of 9 separate square game tiles, each an exact square seen straight down, flat on a fully transparent background, in a 3 by 3 grid, each centred in its own cell with wide empty transparent gaps between them. No text, no labels, no numbers, no frame round the sheet.

Image 1 is a style reference only: match its palette, materials, wear and rendering exactly, and draw none of its objects.

Style: 1970s-80s "used future" industrial equipment inside one small crew capsule of a space station, owned by an indifferent corporation; compact, lived in and kept. Smooth, heavy, continuous surfaces: NO bolts, NO rivets, NO screw heads anywhere. Light scuffs and worn paint spread evenly, with no single distinctive mark that would show when a tile repeats — no grime, no rust, no oil. Every wheel and handle is grey steel; red appears nowhere. Colours dull and desaturated. Crisp game-asset rendering, lighting from the top left.

These are the caps on top of the capsule's low bulkhead walls: one long continuous smooth dull dark yellow steel cap running along each wall, as if cast in one piece. Along every edge where the wall ends, a smooth rounded grey steel edge trim with no bolts. Every edge where the wall continues into the next tile has no trim, no seam and no line at all: the yellow cap runs straight out of the edge into the next tile. Each tile fills its square edge to edge.

Tiles in reading order (row 1 left to right, then row 2, then row 3):
1. Post: trim on all four edges.
2. End: the wall continues through the right edge only; trim along the top, the left and the bottom.
3. Straight: continues through the left and right edges; trim along the top and the bottom.
4. Straight with a seam: as 3, with one fine flush joint line across its middle from the top trim to the bottom trim.
5. Straight, as 3, a little more worn along its middle.
6. Corner: continues through the right and the bottom edges; trim along the top and the left, rounding the corner, a small rounded trim notch at the bottom-right corner.
7. Tee: continues through the left, right and bottom edges; trim along the top only, small notches at the two bottom corners.
8. Cross: continues through all four edges; no trim, small notches at the four corners.
9. Straight, as 3, with a small flush round inspection cap in its middle.
